title: Mock 2 · Building Blocks
blurb: Core rules and dates: IAASB, SCORES, ad approvals, CSCRF basics and the IA code.

questions.q: Under which regulatory framework will SEBI's proposed new asset class be structured?
questions.explanation: The deck states the new asset class will be structured under the MF framework, with relaxed prudential norms and adequate safeguards.
hints: Although the ticket size is closer to PMS, it is not under the PMS framework.
Correct: it sits under the MF framework.
AIFs are not mentioned as its framework.
REIT regulations are unrelated.

questions.q: Under one eligibility route, a mutual fund can offer the new asset class if it has:
options: At least 10 years of operation, irrespective of AUM
At least 1 year of operation and ₹1,000 crore AUM
At least 3 years of operation and ₹10,000 crore AUM
At least 5 years of operation and ₹1 lakh crore AUM
questions.explanation: Eligibility: mutual funds with at least three years of operation and ₹10,000 crore in AUM qualify under one route.
hints: AUM is part of the criterion; 10 years is not mentioned.
1 year and ₹1,000 crore are too low.
Correct: 3 years plus ₹10,000 crore AUM.
5 years and ₹1 lakh crore are not the thresholds.

questions.q: Which of the following assets would typically be held by an InvIT?
options: Highways, power transmission lines and telecom towers
questions.explanation: InvITs own, operate or finance income-generating infrastructure projects like roads, power transmission or telecom towers.
hints: Correct: infrastructure assets.
Offices and malls are commercial real estate held by REITs.
Listed bank shares are equity, not infrastructure.
Bullion is a commodity, not infrastructure.

questions.q: What happened to the indexation benefit on long-term capital gains under the Union Budget 2024 proposals?
options: It was extended to all equity shares
It was made available only to non-residents
questions.explanation: The deck lists 'removal of indexation benefit' as one of the Budget 2024 changes; the takeaway notes this simplifies calculations.
hints: There is no 'doubling' of indexation.
Indexation was not extended; it was removed.
No such non-resident-only rule is mentioned.
Correct: indexation was removed.

questions.q: The holding period for long-term capital gains on REITs and InvITs was changed by Budget 2024 from:
questions.explanation: Time for long-term capital gains on REITs and InvITs was reduced from 3 years to 1 year.
hints: Correct: 3 years to 1 year.
The new period is 1 year, not 2.
The earlier period was 3 years, not 2.
It was reduced, not increased.

questions.q: BSE's recognition as IAASB and RAASB under the SEBI circular of July 12, 2024 is for what period?
questions.explanation: The circular grants recognition for a period of five years starting from July 25, 2024.
hints: Neither 10 years nor April 1 is mentioned.
Both the period and start date are wrong.
Correct: 5 years from July 25, 2024.
The recognition is time-bound, not indefinite.

questions.q: The annual compliance audit of an investment adviser must be completed within what time from the end of each financial year?
questions.explanation: IAs must conduct a yearly compliance audit by an ICAI/ICSI member within six months from the end of each financial year.
hints: Three months is not the audit deadline.
One month is the deadline for submitting adverse findings after the audit report.
Twelve months is too long.
Correct: within six months of FY end.

questions.q: When an investor lodges a complaint against an IA on SCORES, it is automatically forwarded to the IA and simultaneously to:
questions.explanation: The complaint against the IA is simultaneously forwarded to the Designated Body, i.e. BSE, which ensures the ATR is submitted within 21 days.
hints: NISM has no role in grievance redressal.
Correct: BSE as Designated Body gets it at the same time.
The RoC does not handle investor complaints against IAs.
Banks are not part of the SCORES flow.

questions.q: Who set up the Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) portal for the Indian securities market?
questions.explanation: The deck states that MIIs have set up an ODR portal, and IAs must enrol on it.
hints: RBI is not involved.
IA associations did not set it up.
NISM is a training body.
Correct: MIIs set up the ODR portal.

questions.q: How many advertisements can an investment adviser upload for BSE approval in a single application?
questions.explanation: The process slide states the IA can upload up to 3 advertisements for approval in one application.
hints: Correct: up to 3 per application.
More than one is allowed.
5 exceeds the stated limit.
10 exceeds the stated limit.

questions.q: Which type of recommendation is specifically prohibited in IA advertisements?
options: BTST (Buy Today Sell Tomorrow) and ATST (Acquire Today Sell Tomorrow)
questions.explanation: Prohibitions include recommendations such as BTST and ATST, and any recommendation/promotion of a specific investment, scrip or contract.
hints: Portfolio review is a normal service.
Diversification messaging is not prohibited.
Correct: BTST/ATST are expressly prohibited.
Goal-based allocation is sound advice, not a prohibited ad claim.

questions.q: Which of the following advertisements does NOT require BSE's approval?
options: A social-media campaign soliciting new clients
A newspaper ad describing the IA's model portfolio
An ad promoting a new fee plan to prospective clients
questions.explanation: Wishes/greetings on events or festivals are listed among exempted advertisements requiring no BSE approval.
hints: Soliciting clients needs approval.
Correct: festival greetings are exempt.
A model portfolio ad needs approval (and must avoid past performance).
Promoting a fee plan is an advertisement needing approval.

questions.q: Under the SEBI circular of April 06, 2023, which statement about the SEBI logo is correct for investment advisers?
options: The SEBI logo may be used after BSE approval
The SEBI logo shall not be used by an IA
The SEBI logo must appear on all client agreements
The SEBI logo may be used only on the website
questions.explanation: The circular slide notes: 'Please note that SEBI logo shall not be used by IA.'
hints: BSE approval does not permit SEBI logo use.
Correct: an IA cannot use the SEBI logo at all.
Agreements must show registration details, not the SEBI logo.
Even the website cannot carry it.

questions.q: How are individual investment advisers treated under CSCRF?
options: They are excluded from submission of compliance with CSCRF
They must obtain ISO 27001 within 1 year
They are treated as Mid-size REs
They are treated as Qualified REs
questions.explanation: The categorisation slide states individual IAs shall be excluded from submission of compliance with CSCRF.
hints: Correct: individual IAs are excluded from submission.
ISO 27001 within 1 year applies to Qualified REs.
Mid-size does not apply to individual IAs.
Qualified REs are the largest entities.

questions.q: How often must Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) be conducted under CSCRF?
questions.explanation: VAPT must be carried out annually and commenced at the beginning of the financial year; the applicability table shows annual VAPT for all categories.
hints: VAPT is periodic, not event-driven.
3 years is too infrequent.
Correct: annually for all categories.
Quarterly is not the VAPT periodicity.

questions.q: The CSCRF cyber audit must be carried out by:
options: A CERT-In empanelled IS auditing organisation
questions.explanation: Cyber audit is to be carried out by a CERT-In empanelled IS auditing organisation as per SEBI's guidelines.
hints: BSE does not conduct the CSCRF cyber audit.
A CA alone is not the prescribed cyber auditor.
Self-audit by internal IT is not permitted for the cyber audit.
Correct: CERT-In empanelled IS auditor.

questions.q: An entity is registered with SEBI in two capacities that fall in different CSCRF categories. Which provisions apply?
options: Those of the category with more clients
Those of the highest category it falls under
questions.explanation: If an RE is registered under more than one category, the provisions of the highest category under which it falls apply.
hints: Client count alone does not decide it.
The lowest category is not used.
There is no choice.
Correct: the highest category applies.

questions.q: Which principle of the IA Code of Conduct requires seeking information on a client's financial situation, investment experience and objectives, and keeping it confidential?
questions.explanation: 'Information about clients': an IA shall seek from its clients information about their financial situation, investment experience and objectives, and maintain its confidentiality.
hints: Senior management responsibility covers standards in body corporates.
Fair charges is about fees.
Correct: Information about clients.
Capabilities is about resources and procedures.

questions.q: Under the PIT Regulations code, how often at minimum must the compliance officer report to the board or the Audit Committee chairman?
options: Not less than once a year
questions.explanation: The compliance officer reports at the frequency stipulated by the board, but not less than once in a year.
hints: Correct: at least once a year.
Quarterly is not the prescribed minimum.
Reporting is periodic, not only on violations.
Monthly is not the prescribed minimum.

questions.q: According to the Investor Charter, with which registries must an IA register?
options: KYC Registration Agency (KRA) and Central KYC Registry (CKYC)
Registrar of Companies and GST portal only
questions.explanation: The charter lists: 'To obtain registration with Know Your Client Registration Agency (KRA) and Central Know Your Customer Registry (CKYC).'
hints: Depositories/exchanges are not the KYC registries named.
Correct: KRA and CKYC.
These are not the KYC registries named.
AMFI and NISM are not KYC registries.

questions.q: In the monthly complaints disclosure format, how is 'average resolution time' computed?
options: Days the oldest complaint has been pending
Total days taken to resolve each complaint in the month ÷ number of complaints resolved in the month
Complaints pending for more than 3 months ÷ total complaints
questions.explanation: Average resolution time is the sum of time taken to resolve each complaint in days in the current month divided by the total complaints resolved in that month.
hints: The oldest pending complaint is not an average.
Correct: sum of resolution days ÷ complaints resolved.
This is a ratio of ageing, not resolution time.
This mixes received complaints with calendar days.

questions.q: Which bias is also called 'myside bias'?
questions.explanation: Confirmation bias, also called myside bias, is the tendency to search for or interpret information to confirm one's existing beliefs.
hints: Ownership bias is the endowment effect.
Gambler's fallacy predicts random events from the past.
Correct: confirmation bias = myside bias.
Recency bias overweights recent results.

questions.q: 'It is better for reputations to fail conventionally than to succeed unconventionally' (Keynes) is quoted in the module to explain which bias?
questions.explanation: The module uses Keynes's line to explain why most individuals don't go against the crowd: herd mentality.
hints: Correct: herd mentality.
Myopic loss aversion is about loss sensitivity and frequent checking.
Winner's curse is overpaying in a bid.
Anchoring is about the first piece of information.

questions.q: Under a constant-weighting strategic asset allocation:
options: Weights are left to drift as prices move
A minimum portfolio value is protected
Weights change based on momentum signals
Weights are periodically rebalanced to the original or desired levels
questions.explanation: Constant-weighting: weights are periodically rebalanced to the original/desired levels.
hints: That is drifting allocation.
A protected floor describes insured allocation.
Momentum-based changes are tactical/dynamic.
Correct: periodic rebalancing to target.

questions.q: Which asset allocation strategy aims to ensure a minimum portfolio value, usually by adjusting the mix as market conditions worsen?
questions.explanation: Insured asset allocation ensures a minimum portfolio value by allocating assets so a certain level of capital is protected, adjusting as markets worsen.
hints: Correct: insured asset allocation.
Integrated combines SAA and dynamic strategies around evolving goals.
Drifting simply lets weights move.
Constant-weighting rebalances to fixed targets.
